output.summary: When you create a task, the title travels through three places. POST /api/tasks in server/api.js asks taskTitle in server/validation.js to trim spaces and allow only 1-80 characters. If the result is missing, the API returns an error and nothing is saved. If it passes, that clean title is handed to the store in db/store.js, which inserts it into the tasks list.

glossary.meaning: Short check that cleans up extra spaces and allows only titles between 1 and 80 characters long.
The create-task inbox: a message sent to /api/tasks that carries a title to be saved.
A helper that saves tasks and can list them or mark one as done.

output.title: How taskTitle handles padded input for POST tasks
output.prompt: What does taskTitle("  Write report  ") return after trimming and the 1-80 length check, and how does POST /api/tasks use that result?
reviewPoints: server/validation.js: 'const title = value.trim();' plus 'return title;' shows padded input becomes 'Write report' - grounds trimmed return.
server/validation.js: 'if (title.length < 1 || title.length > 80) return null;' shows 12-char trimmed value passes, only empty or >80 returns null.
server/api.js: 'const title = taskTitle(body?.title);' plus 'return { status: 201, data: store.add(title) };' shows accepted trimmed value is passed to store.

options.text: Returns 'Write report' and POST /api/tasks passes it to store.add(title) to create the task.
Returns null as invalid because leading spaces fail validation, so POST returns 400.
Returns the original padded string unchanged and POST stores it with spaces included.
Returns true to signal validity and POST then reads body.title again for storage.

output.answerExplanation: Input is a string, trim removes surrounding spaces to 'Write report' (12 chars) which passes 1-80 check, so it returns the trimmed title. api.js then calls store.add(title) on success.

output.summary: This tiny module exports one test: is this value a real Array? If JavaScript already provides Array.isArray it uses that native check, otherwise it falls back to seeing if the value's type string is '[object Array]'. Tests show true for plain arrays, even with extra properties, and false for objects, array-like objects, strings, numbers, functions, null and undefined.

checks.observation: How does the toString.call fallback compare to the ECMAScript Array.isArray definition for edge cases like cross-realm values?

glossary.meaning: Built-in JavaScript check that returns true only for real arrays, not for plain objects.
Replacement code used when the built-in check is missing, so older setups behave the same.
A plain object that looks like an array because it has numbered keys, but is not a real array.

output.title: Fallback check for array with extra property
output.prompt: Using the fallback function defined in index.js, what should the check return for an array with an added property created by arr = []; arr.foo = 'bar'?
reviewPoints: index.js quote "return toString.call(arr) === '[object Array]';" — grounds that extra property does not change tag, so expected true.
test.js quote "arr.foo = 'bar';" with t.ok(isArray(arr)) — grounds boundary that arrays with custom props stay true, while obj[0]=true stays false.

options.text: true, because the internal tag stays '[object Array]' despite the extra property
false, because adding a named property converts an array to a plain object
false, because the fallback rejects values with non-numeric properties
undefined, because the fallback only handles strings and plain objects

output.answerExplanation: The fallback uses `toString.call(arr) === '[object Array]'`. Adding `foo` does not change that tag, so it returns true, matching the test expectation that `arr.foo='bar'` is still an array.

output.summary: is-number decides if an input counts as a usable finite number. Real numbers pass when num - num is zero, which filters out NaN and Infinity. Strings pass only when not blank after trimming and converting to a finite number. All other values like empty text, words, arrays, objects, booleans, null and undefined return false.

glossary.meaning: A regular usable number, excluding Infinity, -Infinity and NaN.
Text like '1', '0.1' or '5e3' that becomes a finite number when converted with +num.
First checking that trimmed text is not empty, so blanks like '   ' are rejected in index.js.

output.summary: To make a task, you send a title to POST /api/tasks. The app first cleans the title by removing edge spaces, then keeps it only if it is text with 1 to 80 characters left. If valid, the cleaned title is passed to the store, which saves it and returns the new task. If not valid, the app returns an error and nothing is saved.

glossary.meaning: A small checker that removes spaces from the ends of the sent text and keeps it only if 1 to 80 characters remain.
The create-task web address; sending data here asks the app to make a new task.
The save helper that adds the accepted title to the task list and returns the new task.
